findings.title: Atomic file write contract violated under concurrent access
findings.summary: The atomic state persistence subsystem (src/audit/io/artifacts.ts, src/audit/io/runArtifacts.ts) claims atomic writes via temp-file-then-rename pattern. However, the lock acquisition is not atomic with the write operation. Two processes can both acquire the lock (via separate lock files), then both write, with the last writer winning. This violates the single-writer invariant. Counterexample: Process A acquires lock-A, Process B acquires lock-B (different lock files), both write to same target, last rename wins, losing A's changes. The contract should require a single global lock file with atomic creation (O_EXCL flag) and proper cleanup on crash.

findings.title: Symlink and relative path traversal vulnerability in worktree remediation write-scope isolation
findings.summary: The remediation pipeline relies on git worktree isolation and write-scope validation to ensure subagent fixes modify files strictly within designated temporary worktrees. However, write-scope enforcement operates on string-based path comparisons without fully canonicalizing target paths against real filesystem boundaries or resolving pre-existing symlinks. If an LLM subagent generates file mutation instructions containing relative path traversals (../), references symlinks pointing outside the git repository root, or targets internal repository configuration paths (such as .git/hooks), the write-scope guard permits modifications outside the target worktree, creating a severe risk of host file corruption or arbitrary code execution during automated fix application.

Each ships its own state machine: poll → parse → update sliding window → decay → reconcile. Adding a new provider requires re-implementing the entire state machine, and quota bugs (like the deadlock in existing finding #5) must be fixed in N places. The categorically better approach is one ProviderQuotaPoller<Source, Quota> interface where each provider only contributes a *protocol adapter* (request format + response parser), and the shared machinery owns state, decay, and reconciliation. This collapses 10 implementations to 10 thin adapters and centralizes the runtime quota contract. findings.title: Context window saturation and prompt truncation in deep dependency graph context expansion

findings.title: Per-target CLI process spawning in static analyzer adapters should be unified into batched execution pools
findings.summary: Static analysis adapters independently spawn external binary CLI processes (astGrep, eslint, semgrep, codeql) per file chunk or target directory. Spawning thousands of short-lived child processes creates heavy OS process creation overhead, IPC serialization bottlenecks, and CPU thrashing during full repository scans. Consolidating tool executions into batched multi-file worker runs or using persistent worker daemons with stdio streams drastically reduces overall analysis latency and resource consumption.

findings.title: Redundant duplicate graph partitioning across review packet creation and task graph scheduling
findings.summary: The task orchestration subsystem executes two independent graph clustering and partitioning passes over the same codebase graph dependencies. During initial planning, src/audit/orchestrator/reviewPacketGraphClustering.ts builds clusters to group files into review packets. Subsequently, src/audit/orchestrator/partitionTaskGraph.ts re-evaluates dependency edges and computes graph partitions using src/audit/orchestrator/taskAffinityGraph.ts to group tasks into execution waves. Both passes perform costly depth-first traversals and affinity calculations on identical dependency slices (dependencySlices.ts). Collapsing packet graph clustering and task graph partitioning into a single unified topological cluster topology eliminates O(V+E) graph re-traversals and ensures uniform execution boundaries throughout the audit pipeline.

findings.title: Unbounded subprocess stdio buffering and process group leaks during tool execution
findings.summary: Process spawning across spawn-shell.mjs and localCommands.ts relies on custom stdio buffering and subprocess management. Under large repository scale or heavy analyzer output, stdio buffers can exceed default Node.js buffer limits (ERR_CHILD_PROCESS_STDIO_MAXBUFFER), causing process crashes. Furthermore, spawned child processes are not grouped into process trees, leaving orphan background analyzer processes running upon cancellation. Replacing bespoke process wrappers with standard libraries like Execa resolves buffer streaming and signal propagation.

findings.title: Concurrent planAssignments calls share mutable lastUnplaceableNodeIds instance
findings.summary: lastUnplaceableNodeIds is a plain instance field read by unplaceableNodeIds() after planAssignments() returns. If a second driver concurrently invokes planAssignments, the field is overwritten — unplaceableNodeIds() then reports the SECOND plan's unplaceables, not the one the caller is consulting. This is a real cross-driver race the file's own header says cannot drift between drivers.
evidence: src/shared/dispatch/coordinator.ts:147-158 - lastUnplaceableNodeIds is shared mutable state with no per-call identity. A second concurrent planAssignments() call between plan N's completion and caller N reading unplaceableNodeIds() corrupts caller N's view. The class is constructed once and shared by both drivers (per the CE-001 comment), so the race is reachable whenever both drivers run concurrently.

findings.title: Precompute and cache analyzer capability matrix instead of probing at runtime
findings.summary: Static analyzer adapters (src/audit/adapters/astGrep.ts, codeql.ts, eslint.ts, semgrep.ts) and the shared analyzer acquisition engine (src/shared/analyzers/) probe for tool availability, versions, and capabilities at runtime on every audit run. Instead, generate a static capability manifest at install time (scripts/audit/postinstall.mjs) that records which analyzers are available, their versions, and supported languages. The runtime then reads this manifest instead of probing, and only re-probes when the manifest is missing or stale. This changes the work from dynamic probing to static lookup, reducing startup latency and making runs more deterministic.

findings.title: Replace full git history parsing with incremental commit-graph delta updates
findings.summary: src/audit/extractors/gitHistory.ts and src/audit/orchestrator/gitHistoryBaseline.ts re-run full git log and git blame subprocesses on every intake, even for repositories that have only changed slightly since the last run. findings.title: resolveFromPath resolves separator-paths against process cwd but they spawn against root
findings.summary: The separator/absolute branch of resolveFromPath returns the bare command string whenever existsSync(command) passes, and existsSync on a relative path is evaluated against the process CWD (line 45), while runFirstAvailableCommand later spawns with cwd: root (line 121). A slash-relative candidate (e.g. "scripts/helper.js") therefore RESOLVES relative to the process directory but EXECUTES relative to root — whenever the two differ (a slash-command launched from a subdirectory of the audited root), a different file than the one resolved can be spawned, or the resolve succeeds but the spawn ENOENTs.

findings.title: reconcile() prunes-then-writes even when no removal occurred
findings.summary: reconcile always calls writeRecordMap after pruning, regardless of whether anything was actually removed. If prune dropped leases but reconciliation removed none, the function still writes. Today it is a hidden write amplification.

Every other async-sensitive test in this file bounds `run()` with a `Promise.race` deadline (5s at line 971-974, 15s at 2029-2034, 2091-2096, 2136-2141, 2205-2210, 2266-2271, 2300-2305, 2334-2339, 2381-2386, 2417-2422) so a regression that wedges the engine fails loudly; this test has no such guard, so a backfill regression hangs the entire shared suite indefinitely.
evidence: tests/shared/rollingDispatch.test.ts:450-458 - `while (!done) {... await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 15));}` poll loop with no deadline against an unbounded `runPromise`
tests/shared/rollingDispatch.test.ts:459 - `const results = await runPromise;` is awaited bare — no `Promise.race` guard
tests/shared/rollingDispatch.test.ts:971-974 - The livelock test for the same class of regression wraps run() in `Promise.race([... setTimeout(reject, 5000)])`, the pattern this test lacks

findings.title: Constructor's defaultTtlMs = STALE_LOCK_MS but DISPATCH_LEASE_TTL_MS overrides at the call site — two TTLs
findings.summary: The class default is the fileLock STALE_LOCK_MS, but the documented correct TTL for live LLM dispatches is DISPATCH_LEASE_TTL_MS (20 min). The default is therefore the WRONG TTL for the documented use case — every caller must remember to pass leaseTtlMs: DISPATCH_LEASE_TTL_MS. The constructor could default to DISPATCH_LEASE_TTL_MS and let the per-op override cover the rare short-TTL use.
evidence: src/shared/quota/reservationLedger.ts:256-267 + DISPATCH_LEASE_TTL_MS at line 47 - The constructor default is STALE_LOCK_MS (the fileLock's stale-cleanup interval), but the only documented correct TTL for live dispatches is DISPATCH_LEASE_TTL_MS. Today the dispatch loop must remember to pass leaseTtlMs, otherwise it uses the wrong TTL. Defaulting to DISPATCH_LEASE_TTL_MS would be the safer contract.

findings.title: getReservationLedgerPath() fallback path uses process.pid in filename — tempdir leak under restarts
findings.summary: When getQuotaStatePath() throws (the catch branch), the fallback creates a per-PID file in tmpdir(). If the process crashes, the tmpdir file is never reconciled, never expired, and pid-reuse can collide. PIDs on Linux can wrap; on Windows PID reuse is also reachable. A long-lived quota state dir misconfiguration produces accumulating tmpdir garbage.
evidence: src/shared/quota/reservationLedger.ts:412-422 - the fallback uses process.pid for filename uniqueness, but: (1) tmpdir() is not pruned, so each crashed process leaves a stale file; (2) PID reuse means a subsequent process can pick up another process's orphan ledger and treat its leases as live until they expire (20 min). Better: include a per-process random suffix, OR reuse the same path across processes (the ledger is shared anyway), OR document that the fallback intentionally degrades to per-process isolation.

findings.title: Deep-nested hand-rolled bracket scanner in extractArtifactsWritten is brittle and hard to maintain
findings.summary: extractArtifactsWritten (seam-dependency-map-executor-writeset-parity.test.ts) recreates the executors' artifacts_written lists with ~60 lines of regex + a hand-written bracket-depth matching loop over raw TypeScript source. It relies on the exact textual layout of executor files (inline literals, a specific `const X = [...]` then `artifacts_written: X` pattern) and any executor that assembles its write-set differently silently drops artifacts from the parity check, so the test's correctness depends on keeping this mini-parser in sync with how executors write their arrays.

findings.title: Malformed JSON-candidate stderr lines silently dropped with no accounting
findings.summary: collectClaudeCodeJsonLines silently discards every `{`-prefixed stderr line that fails JSON.parse (e.g. a truncated object from a chunked stream), losing rate-limit/header signal with no counter or log — a broken claude-code contract is invisible to operators.

affected_files.quoted_text: parsed = JSON.parse(trimmed);

evidence: src/shared/quota/claudeCodeJsonLines.ts:22-27 - try/catch around JSON.parse with "// Not valid JSON — skip" drops every malformed `{`-prefixed line; nothing counts or reports the drop rate, so a server that starts emitting truncated objects degrades quota pacing silently

findings.title: Sentinel-absence guard is a low-signal .not.toBe assertion
findings.summary: The 'nextMissingContractPhase never returns the old sentinel' regression test asserts the removed-phase sentinel is never returned via .not.toBe("obligation_ledger_phase") in two places (line 431 and line 442). An absence assertion of this form passes for any incorrect phase value that is not the exact sentinel string, so it would not catch a regression that returns a different wrong phase; only the paired positive assertions actually carry signal.

affected_files.quoted_text: expect(nextMissingContractPhase(ARTIFACTS_DIR)).not.toBe("obligation_ledger_phase");

evidence: tests/remediate/contract-pipeline.test.ts:431 - absence-only guard for a deleted sentinel string; passes for any non-sentinel wrong value
tests/remediate/contract-pipeline.test.ts:442 - second identical .not.toBe absence assertion, same low-signal shape

themes.title: Observed atomicity and lifecycle failures
themes.root_cause: Operational state transitions rely on prechecks, process-local bookkeeping, and best-effort cleanup instead of atomic ownership changes and fail-closed settlement, so concurrent admission, rollback, timeout, and recovery paths can lose state or strand work.
themes.suggested_fix_pattern: Model each lifecycle as one transactional state machine: use atomic compare-and-set or exclusive locks for admission and persistence, stable ownership tokens, idempotent rollback, finally-based lease reconciliation, and hard watchdog settlement with startup recovery.

themes.title: Conceptual automation trust-boundary gaps
themes.root_cause: The automation design lets untrusted repository content and model-directed actions cross prompt, filesystem, and process boundaries without a unified containment model based on canonical paths, instruction-data separation, and least privilege.
themes.suggested_fix_pattern: Create one hardened worker boundary that realpath-canonicalizes and allowlists every write, excludes repository control paths, treats repository text as explicitly untrusted data, runs workers in an OS-level sandbox with minimal permissions, and verifies containment with adversarial end-to-end tests.

themes.title: Conceptual duplication and split sources of truth
themes.root_cause: Audit and Remediate repeatedly encode the same orchestration, quota, validation, command, repository-context, and artifact concepts in parallel modules, making cross-cutting contracts convention-based and allowing behavior to drift between implementations.
themes.suggested_fix_pattern: Consolidate shared mechanics into small typed declarative kernels: one step executor, provider-quota protocol adapter, grounding pipeline, command registry, canonical repository context, and artifact descriptor catalog; replace custom parsers and graph primitives with mature libraries where appropriate.

themes.title: Observed false-green and stale-evidence gates
themes.root_cause: Success predicates validate only selected failure representations and tests often stop at helpers or encode permissive expectations, so missing results, nonstandard CI failures, deferred verification errors, and source changes can pass as complete and current.
themes.suggested_fix_pattern: Define an exhaustive fail-closed completion predicate shared by reporting and closeout, bind evidence to content hashes and cross-artifact identities, and exercise complete orchestration paths with tests that inject missing, timed-out, startup-failed, deferred-failed, and stale inputs.

themes.title: Observed artifact identity and integrity drift
themes.root_cause: Persisted artifacts and aggregation steps lack sufficiently strong completeness, version, checksum, range, and survivor-state invariants, allowing partial snapshots, corrupt state, invalid numeric data, or removed dedupe nodes to erase or distort evidence.
themes.suggested_fix_pattern: Use versioned and checksummed envelopes with atomic fsync-backed replacement and last-known-good recovery, validate snapshot completeness and schema bounds before replacement, and make aggregation operate only on explicit live survivors with conservation-of-evidence assertions.

executive_summary: Across 2,241 finalized findings from 200 work blocks, the dominant observed failure mode is non-atomic lifecycle and validation logic: concurrent state, recovery, lease, and closeout paths can lose work, hang, or report green after failure. Separately, the conceptual design critique identifies duplicated orchestration, quota, provider, validation, and command layers as the mechanism that allows those contracts to drift. The highest-impact boundary risk combines untrusted repository prompt content, path containment gaps, and permission-free autonomous workers, creating a credible route from audit input to host-level modification.
top_risks: Observed contract risk: concurrent writes, non-atomic admission, and failed rollback can lose durable state, exceed declared capacity, or release a poisoned remediation base (REL-4802dc9e, REL-849efef5, REL-66feeed3).

Conceptual trust-boundary risk: prompt injection, path traversal, and permission-free workers can convert a hostile target repository into host-level file or process compromise (ARC-e5288553, ARC-b3f6ac48, SEC-353f7027).

Observed correctness risk: incomplete test runs, unsuccessful CI conclusions, deferred verification failures, and stale findings can all be accepted as green or current (COR-38d1cc15, COR-7b37298d, COR-f93dac11, COR-e0f110ff).

Conceptual architecture risk: parallel orchestrators, quota engines, validators, and command contexts multiply contract drift and make systemic fixes inconsistent (ARC-8aa0073d, OPR-e79ede8c, TST-182085b7, ARC-2789fce7).
Observed data-integrity risk: corrupt or partial artifacts and invalid dedupe transitions can erase progress or evidence without a reliable recovery path (DAT-d0cebdda, DAT-eb3aeddf, COR-ccf4eccd).
